chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Ibn Rabat, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A man divorces his wife with one divorce while he is sick, and he had previously divorced her with two divorces.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She inherits him if it is during his illness.' I said, 'And what is the limit of the illness?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He remains sick until he dies, and if that is prolonged, up to a year.'
ai.seo_question: Does a sick man's divorce prevent his wife from inheriting him if he dies from that illness?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling of 'marad al-mawt' (death illness) in Shia jurisprudence, establishing that a single divorce during such an illness does not sever inheritance rights, thereby protecting the wife's financial security. It defines the threshold for this illness not by severity but by duration, extending the status until death or potentially up to a year, reflecting the juristic principle that the finality of death is the key determinant for inheritance eligibility.
